title: Appendix I.3: Test Data Catalog and Evidence
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Appendix I.3 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **test data catalog** provides safe **sample customers, vehicles, products and payment data** for training, tests and screenshots and documents the **evidence** per test case. This guide shows how to **select** test data and file **evidence**.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Catalog
bullets: Test vehicles per division with VIN, model series, OTR deal ID
Test products, campaigns, bank details (test accounts)

sections.head: Evidence
bullets: Reference to ticket and chapter (Appendix E)

steps: Select the customer, vehicle and product from the **catalog** to match the test case or practical example.
Run the test case in the **test or training system**; use only test accounts for bank details.
Document the **evidence**: test case, date, release, environment, result.

right.text: ~~Real customer, vehicle or bank data are not test data.~~ Test data come exclusively from the catalog; production data are not permitted in tests and images (Chapter 16.1).

steps: Also use test data for **screenshots** (Appendix G) and **Product Testing** (Chapter 14.12).
Report unusable or missing test data to the editorial team (Appendix F).

bullets: Test case or practical example (Appendix I.1)
☐  Test data selected from the catalog
☐  Test case run in the test system
Test vehicles are available per division with matching identifiers (Chapter 21.2).
Evidence is a prerequisite for the productive functional baseline (Chapter 16.4).
The catalog is updated with each release (Chapter 22).

qa: May I create a real vehicle in the training system?
No, only test vehicles from the catalog.
Where do I file the evidence?
In the evidence register of the catalog with reference to test case and release.
Are there test data for tyre contracts?
Yes, test products with tyre type and tyre size (Chapter 13).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __Test data catalog and evidence__ – Appendix I.3.

title: T6-7: From Saved Application to Payment Data and Signature
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T6-7 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module links **Chapter 6** (application saved, reference number available) with **Chapter 7** (payment data, documents, signature). You check what must be in place at the **transition** and avoid the typical breaks between application and signature.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Starting point (Chapter 6)
bullets: Special approval identified or not required

sections.head: Target (Chapter 7)
bullets: Payment method, interval, payer and invoice recipient entered

steps: Open the saved application via the **reference number** (Chapter 8.1) and check the **application status**.
Make sure the application is **complete**: an application with open validation cannot proceed to signature.
Switch to the **customer data check** and activate the **collective invoice** if required (Chapters 6 and 7.2).

right.text: ~~After "Create application", product, term and mileage can no longer be changed.~~ Errors from Chapter 6 cannot be corrected in the transition; they require a new contract.

steps: Enter **payment method, interval and bank details** (Chapters 7.1 to 7.3).
Generate the **application preview** and click the **check mark** to sign (Chapter 7.4).
Select the **signature type** and check the **signature status** (Chapters 7.5 to 7.8).

bullets: Customer e-mail and mobile number in customer master data
☐  Signature route selected and status checked
The payment interval can later only be changed to "one-time".
With special approvals, activation waits for the MO Check; the signature can still be obtained.
Missing customer contact data block e-mail and SMS signature.

qa: Can I pause between saving and signature?
Yes, the application remains accessible under its reference number in Application Management.
What if the customer wants to change the payment method?
Change it before signature in Chapter 7.1; after signature, a new signature is required (Chapter 7.7).
Does the payer have to sign?
The payer signs the SEPA mandate; the contract holder signs the contract (Chapter 7.2).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __Chapter 6__ – Create service contract and complete application.
__oneSCM Handbook__ – Complete chapters with screenshots, role, status and scope matrices (Appendix D).
**Support and escalation** – Report a support case with reference number, market, division and screenshot (Chapters 23.4 and 23.5).

title: T7-8: From Documents and Signature to Activation Check
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T7-8 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module links **Chapter 7** (signature and documents available) with **Chapter 8** (track and activate application). You make sure that all **activation prerequisites** are met before Customer Management reviews.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Starting point (Chapter 7)
bullets: Documents filed in the system or uploaded

sections.head: Target (Chapter 8)
bullets: First registration and license plate added

steps: Check the **signature and document status** in **Application Management** (Chapters 7.8 and 8.1).
Open the "**Update**" action via "**…**" and add the **first registration date** and **license plate** (Chapter 8.3).
In the "**Communication**" tab, upload the copy of **ZB I/ZB II** and, for the print variant, the signed document.

right.text: ~~Without first registration, license plate and ZB II, no activation takes place~~, even if the application is signed. The upload is not a mandatory field in the system.

steps: Make sure that no **open special approval** is blocking activation (Chapters 6.5 and 9).
Track the **application status** until activation and respond to queries from Customer Management (Chapters 8.6 and 8.7).

bullets: Contract document and SEPA mandate filed
First registration, license plate and ZB II available
☐  First registration and license plate added
With e-signature and e-mail signature, the contract documents are filed automatically; with print, they must be uploaded.
Incorrect applications are rejected; the customer is informed.
The limit of 12 months or 50,000 km after first registration applies (Chapter 23.1).

qa: The customer has signed, but the application is not active. Why?
Usually first registration, license plate or ZB II is missing; see Chapter 8.3.
Can I submit the ZB II later?
Yes, at any time via Application Management › Reference number › Communication.
Who activates the contract?
The system if data are complete, otherwise Customer Management after review (Chapter 8.5).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __oneSCM Handbook__ – Complete chapters with screenshots, role, status and scope matrices (Appendix D).

title: T8-9: Overall Process and MO Role Deep Dive
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T8-9 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module links the **dealer view** of the application (**Chapter 8**) with the **MO view** of the functional review (**Chapter 9**). You understand what the MO reviews, how feedback reaches the dealer and how both roles complete the **overall process** together.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

steps: Place the application in the **overall process**: submitted → under review → approved/rejected → active (Appendix D).
As MO, open the application from the **work list** and check it against the **criteria** (Chapters 9.2 and 9.4).
As dealer, read the **check status** and the **reasons** in the communication (Chapters 8.2 and 9.3).

right.text: ~~Dealer and MO communicate via the application, not via private channels.~~ Reasons and queries belong in the application's communication so they remain traceable.

steps: On **rejection**, the dealer corrects and resubmits; the MO reviews again (Chapters 8.7 and 9.5).
After **approval**, activation takes place; both roles check the result (Chapters 8.6 and 9.6).

bullets: MO role and check criteria known (Chapter 9.1)
Communication channel between dealer and MO clarified
☐  Application status in overall process known
☐  Check criteria clear to both roles
Special approvals from Chapter 12 go through the same MO Check.
Contract Review profiles give the MO the overview (Chapter 9.8).

qa: How does the dealer learn the review result?
Via status and communication in Application Management (Chapter 8.2).
Can the MO correct data directly?
The MO reviews; corrections to the application are made by the dealer (Chapter 9.5).
How long does an MO Check take?
Depends on completeness and work list; complete applications are processed first.
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __oneSCM Handbook__ – Complete chapters with screenshots, role, status and scope matrices (Appendix D).

title: T9-10: From Review Result to Ongoing Contract Administration
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T9-10 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module links the **review result** (**Chapter 9**, approved and activated) with **ongoing contract administration** (**Chapter 10**). You know which data are locked upon activation, what remains changeable in day-to-day work and when changes are re-reviewed.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Starting point (Chapter 9)
bullets: Check status and reasons in the history

steps: After activation, check the **contract details** and the **payment plan** (Chapters 10.1 and 11.1).
Know the **locked data**: product, term, mileage, payment interval (can only be changed to "one-time").
In day-to-day work, use the **permitted actions**: customer and payment data, change of payer, suspension, follow-up quote (Chapters 10.2 to 10.5).

right.text: ~~Activation starts the payment plan and the service entitlement.~~ Changes to product or term are only possible via a new contract; terminations have financial consequences (Chapters 10.6 and 11.6).

steps: Changes requiring review go back into the **MO Check** (Chapter 9.7).
Document every change traceably in the **history** (Chapter 10.8).

bullets: ☐  Contract details and payment plan checked after activation
☐  Change requiring review passed to MO
The review history from Chapter 9 remains visible on the contract.
Transition module T6-7 describes the start, this module the end of the application process.
Reporting on active contracts in Chapter 11.7.

qa: Can the MO revoke an active contract?
No, after activation the rules in Chapter 10.6 for cancellation and termination apply.
Which changes trigger an MO Check?
Change of payer, contract transfer and special conditions (Chapters 9.7 and 10.3).
Where can I see the review result later?
In the change history of the contract (Chapter 10.8).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __oneSCM Handbook__ – Complete chapters with screenshots, role, status and scope matrices (Appendix D).
**Support and escalation** – Report a support case with reference number, market, division and screenshot (Chapters 23.4 and 23.5).

title: T14-15: Linking Market Maintenance and Central Requirements
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T14-15 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module links **market maintenance** (**Chapter 14**) with the **central requirements of HQ** (**Chapter 15**). You know which maintenance decisions the market makes alone, which need **HQ approval** and how **country deviations** are requested.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Market decides (Chapter 14)
bullets: Price versions, campaigns, discounts within the Blueprint

sections.head: HQ decides (Chapter 15)
bullets: Technical options, SA matching, coverage codes

steps: Classify the planned change: **within the Blueprint** (market decides) or **deviation** (HQ approval required).
Prepare the change in **Product Testing** and secure test evidence (Chapters 14.12, 16.4).
Request a **country deviation** from HQ with justification (Chapter 15.3) and enter it in the register (Chapter 20.6).

right.text: ~~No publication of a deviation before HQ approval.~~ Unapproved deviations count as a Blueprint violation and are withdrawn.

steps: Await **HQ approval** before publishing (Chapters 14.7 and 15.4).
Inform **MO and dealers** about effective changes (Chapter 15.5).

bullets: Blueprint and country deviation register known (Chapters 15.2, 20.6)
☐  Change classified as Blueprint or deviation
The counterpart T15-14 describes the handover of central foundations to the market.
Coverage codes and technical options affect all markets (Chapter 15.7).
Approvals are kept traceable in the clarification register (Appendix F).

qa: May the market create a campaign without HQ?
Yes, within the Blueprint (Chapter 14.13); deviating conditions need HQ approval.
How long does HQ approval take?
According to the HQ governance process (Chapter 15.4); the status is in the register.
What happens on rejection?
The change remains unpublished; the market can request again with a new justification.
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __Chapter 14__ – Market role, product and price maintenance.
__Chapter 15__ – HQ role, Blueprint and central master data.

title: T15-14: Handing Over Central Foundations to Market Maintenance
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T15-14 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module describes the path from **HQ** (**Chapter 15**) to the **market** (**Chapter 14**): how Blueprint changes, new **products**, **coverage codes** and **technical options** are provided centrally and **adopted, configured locally and published** by the market.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: HQ provides (Chapter 15)
bullets: Product definitions, coverage codes, technical options
Requirements for price components and factor limits

steps: Read the HQ **release information**: what changes in the Blueprint, and from when does it apply (Chapter 22.4)?
Adopt **product definitions** and **coverage codes** into market maintenance (Chapters 14.8, 15.7).
Configure locally: **price versions, clusters, vehicle groups, campaigns** (Chapters 14.9 to 14.13).

right.text: ~~Central changes apply from the date named by HQ.~~ A market that delays adoption offers products outside the valid Blueprint.

steps: Test in **Product Testing** and document the **functional acceptance** (Chapters 14.12, 17.3).
**Publish** and inform MO and dealers; update training materials (Chapters 14.7, 22.3).

bullets: Approved Blueprint change or new product (Chapter 15.2)
Counterpart to T14-15 (market requests deviation from HQ).
Note the effect of product changes on existing contracts (Chapter 14.10).
Division reference: Vans model series clustering (Chapter 14.11).

qa: Does the market have to adopt every Blueprint change?
Yes, unless an approved country deviation says otherwise (Chapter 15.3).
Who maintains the prices for a new product?
The market in its price versions (Chapter 14.9) based on the HQ requirements.
How are dealers informed?
Via the RetailPortal and the release information (Chapter 22.4).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

bullets: __Chapter 15__ – HQ role, Blueprint and central master data.
__Chapter 14__ – Market role, product and price maintenance.
__oneSCM RetailPortal__ – System news and training material.

title: T15-16: From Maintenance Decision to Governance Evidence
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes transition module T15-16 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: This module links the **HQ maintenance decision** (**Chapter 15**) with the **governance evidence** (**Chapter 16**): every decision receives a **source, test evidence, approval and version** so that it can be audited and archived.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Decision (Chapter 15)
bullets: Technical options, SA matching, coverage codes
Governance and approval at HQ level

sections.head: Evidence (Chapter 16)
bullets: Sources, tickets, versions, clarification register, archiving

steps: Document the **decision** with justification, source and ticket reference (Chapter 16.6).
Go through the **approval workflow** with functional review (Chapter 16.3).
File **test evidence** and set the **functional baseline** (Chapter 16.4).

right.text: ~~A decision without evidence is not approved.~~ Only with source, test evidence and documented approval does it become part of the productive functional baseline.

steps: Close open entries in the **clarification register** and update the **version** (Chapter 16.7).
**Archive** the approved version; working documents remain in document management (Chapter 16.5).

bullets: Access to clarification register and version control
☐  Test evidence and functional baseline set
Evidence is the basis for rollout and training (Chapter 17).
Data protection also applies to evidence and test data (Chapter 16.1, Appendix I.3).
The change overview (Chapter 22.4) is fed by this evidence.

qa: What evidence does a coverage code change need?
Source, test evidence per affected division and HQ approval (Chapters 15.7, 16.4).
Who archives?
The editorial team after approval (Chapter 16.5).
How do I find the decision later?
Via version control and the clarification register (Chapter 16.6, Appendix F).
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

__Chapter 16__ – Governance, quality, data protection and archiving.

title: V.1: Welcome and Document Context
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes preface V.1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **preface** explains **who** the oneSCM handbook is written for, **which version** applies, how **variants** per role, market and division are created and how to give **feedback**. This guide is the entry point before all chapters.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

sections.head: Document context
bullets: Target groups: Dealer, MO, Market, HQ
Variants per role, market and division

sections.head: Working with the handbook
bullets: Chapter structure (purpose, prerequisites, steps, result, notes)

steps: Check the **version and date** of the handbook; they appear in the footer of every page.
Select the **variant** for your role, your market and your division.
Get to know the **chapter structure**: purpose, prerequisites, roles, steps, result, special cases, notes, troubleshooting, sources.

right.text: ~~Only the current version of the handbook is valid.~~ Older exports may contain outdated processes; check date and release (Chapter 22.4).

steps: Use the **Quick Guides** as a summary and the handbook for details.
Give **feedback** via the clarification register or the feedback function of the online help (Appendix F).

bullets: Your own role, market and division
Access to the handbook or the online help
The reading path per role is in V.2.
Terms are explained in the glossary (Appendix A).
Data protection rules for examples in Chapter 16.1.

qa: Who is the handbook for?
For all roles in oneSCM: Dealer, MO, Market and HQ, with variants per market and division.
How do I recognize the valid version?
By the date in the footer and the release information (Chapter 22.4).
Where do I give feedback?
Via the clarification register (Appendix F) or the feedback function of the online help.
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers

title: V.2: Table of Contents and Reading Paths
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes preface V.2 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: The **table of contents** shows the 23 chapters, appendices and transition modules; the **reading paths** recommend the order of chapters per **role**. This guide helps you quickly find the right entry point.

left.text: This document is interactive – references to handbook chapters and systems are provided as links.

steps: Select the **reading path for your role** and read the **fundamentals** first (Chapters 1 to 3).
Follow the **process chapters** in the order of the reading path; the **transition modules** link them.
For each chapter, use the **Quick Guide** as a summary and checklist.

right.text: ~~The reading paths are recommendations, not authorizations.~~ Which chapters you may carry out in the system is determined by role and scope (Appendix D).

steps: Consult the **appendices** as needed: glossary, checklists, matrices, practical examples.
Finish with **Chapter 23** (FAQ and support) and the **knowledge check** (Appendix H).

bullets: Fundamentals Chapters 1 to 3 read or scheduled
☐  Reading path for the role selected
☐  Process chapters worked through in order
The dashboard shows the structure and the click path interactively.
Country and division chapters (20, 21) supplement every reading path.
New chapters are added to the reading paths with releases (Chapter 22).

qa: Do I have to read all 23 chapters?
No, the reading path for your role names the relevant chapters; the others are for reference.
Where are the transition modules?
Between the chapters they link, e.g. T6-7 between Chapters 6 and 7.
Are there reading paths per market?
Reading paths apply per role; market specifics are in Chapter 20.
right.title: Frequently asked questions and answers
